blocks.text: Scientists did not accept Lamarck's ideas. When he proposed them there was no evidence to explain the mechanism of evolution, and Lamarck was criticised more for advocating evolutionary change than for the mechanism he proposed. Later, when the mechanisms of inheritance were discovered, Lamarckism was disproved on these grounds:

items: Acquired characters have no genetic basis, so they cannot be inherited by the next generations.
Organs are not modified by the wish or needs of an organism.

blocks.title: Initiating and planning
blocks.text: The book asks you to hypothesise whether Lamarck was criticised in his day for advocating evolution or for the mechanism he proposed. Its own text answers: mostly for advocating the idea of evolutionary change.

blocks.prompt: A weightlifter develops large muscles. Will the children inherit them? Explain.
blocks.explanation: No. The larger muscles are an acquired character with no change in the genes of the sex cells, so they are not inherited; this is the main objection to Lamarckism.

items: Acquired characters have no genetic basis and are not inherited.
Organs are not changed by an organism's wishes or needs.
